title: Keyboard-first trace navigator and live filter scratchpad
content:
Purpose
- Capture quick ideas and interaction rules for a keyboard-first trace viewer mode (fast exploration for power users, accessibility, and keyboard-only debugging in terminals / remote sessions).
- Surface matching filter UI patterns for live-filtering large traces without blocking render.
- Sketch backlog items and edge cases for grooming.

Problem statement / context
- Our current trace viewer is mouse-first. Power users want a keyboard path for rapid span hopping, bookmarking, and filter mutation.
- Accessibility team flagged gaps for screen-reader handoff and focus drift when waterfall columns resize.
- Large traces (10k+ spans) need incremental filtering and virtualized rendering; naive reflows cause jank.

High-level UX goals
- Keyboard-first baseline: arrow/j/k to move selection; enter/space to expand spans; f to open filter palette; / for fuzzy span search; g then t to jump to top; g then b to jump to bottom.
- Persistent caret concept: a focused span is the single source of truth for keyboard ops (caret location) rather than the mouse hover. Caret persists across collapses/expand and timeline zooms.
- Live filter palette: filter combinator UI that supports incremental results (apply-as-you-type) with debounce and partial counts so users get feedback immediately for large traces.
- Snapshots & bookmarks: lightweight bookmark model (B) to pin a caret + zoom + active-filters snapshot. Bookmarks list accessible via keyboard (Shift-B to list).
- Compact lane mode: reduce visual noise for spans without children or telemetry by collapsing to single-line chips; maintain keyboard focus flow.

Wireframe / interaction sketches (verbal)
1) Default keyboard mode layout
 - Left rail: collapsible timeline mini-map + bookmark rail (small icons)
 - Center: waterfall lanes with caret outline on focused span (thicker border, not hover).
 - Right rail: detail flyout that can be toggled (d) and is focus-trap when opened.
 - Bottom: live filter pill row + input when filter palette open.

2) Caret movement rules
 - Up/Down: move to previous/next visible span in DOM order (skip invisible collapsed children).
 - Right: if caret on collapsed parent -> expand and move caret to first child. If on expanded parent -> move to next sibling.
 - Left: collapse if expanded, otherwise move to parent.
 - Home/End or g t / g b: jump trace start/end.
 - PageUp/PageDown: jump by viewport-sized span groups (preserve relative position in nested lanes).

3) Filter palette (f)
 - Keyboard open (f) -> focus input. Palette supports tokens: service:, status:, duration>, trace-id:, tag:. Example: service:api AND duration>200ms.
 - Autocomplete shows sample values and a lightweight count for first 200 results (count is approximate for huge traces).
 - Hitting Enter applies filter incrementally (no full reflow) and updates the visible-span set using virtualization + bloom-filter-backed prefilter stage.
 - Ctrl-Enter applies filter globally (persist to snapshot/bookmark).

4) Fuzzy span search (/)
 - Simple typed search over span name, metadata, log message snippets. Keyboard shows N/ matches and Up/Down to cycle.
 - When cycling, timeline auto-scrolls to center the selected span. Caret follows search selection.

5) Detail flyout & focus behavior
 - d toggles right-hand flyout; when open, focus moves into first actionable element (copy span id, open logs, open logs in timeline).
 - Esc closes flyout and returns caret to previously-focused span.

6) Mini-map interactions
 - Mini-map displays heatmap of latency hotspots, colored by p95. Clicking or keyboard-jumping (m then arrow to zone) moves viewport.
 - Keyboard shortcut m+1..9 to jump to pre-set zones; lowercase m toggles.

Performance & implementation notes (engineering constraints)
- Virtualized DOM essential: only render visible spans plus small buffer.
- Prefilter pipeline: streaming prefilter that scans span meta to produce candidate set quickly (probabilistic counts allowed).
- Incremental layout: avoid expensive relayouts on each filter keystroke. Use layered canvases for waterfall bars and an overlay for caret/highlight to decouple from DOM changes.
- Accessibility: ensure aria-activedescendant driven caret; avoid moving DOM focus for every caret move (use roving tabindex pattern). Screen reader users can open a condensed linear list view that mirrors caret position.
- Telemetry: instrument time-to-first-highlight when filters applied, filter-applied latency histogram, keyboard command usage counters.

Edge cases & unresolved questions
- How to represent collapsed-but-selected parent in compact lane mode? (visual affordance + keyboard hint?)
- Conflict resolution for concurrent bookmarks: if user applies bookmark while another user updates filters (collab), how to surface merge? Likely versioned snapshots with quick revert.
- Should fuzzy search include logs inline or only metadata? Including logs may be slow for large traces; consider optional toggle to include logs.
- Export/Share: keyboard users expect single keystroke to copy permalink to current caret+filters state. Add `y` to copy link?

Backlog items (candidate tickets)
- TRC-1102: Implement caret model + roving tabindex scaffolding (priority p0).
- TRC-1103: Live filter palette UI + streaming prefilter backend (p0).
- TRC-1106: Compact lane render mode + transition animations (p1).
- TRC-1109: Mini-map keyboard zones and heatmap overlay (p2).
- TRC-1114: Accessibility testing & screen-reader condensed list (p0).

Quick prototype tasks (for next sprint)
- Low-fi clickable prototype in Figma: show caret, filter palette, and flyout flows. (owner: Priya)
- Small web prototype that only renders synthetic traces and supports keyboard movement + basic filter apply (owner: Miguel)
- Instrument basic telemetry to capture keyboard usage for initial cohort (owner: Samir)

Notes to self (rough)
- Keep interactions forgiving: if filter returns zero results, show ephemeral suggestion list with likely causes (typos, token not present).
- Consider 'time-slice' mode where filters operate on contiguous time windows rather than whole-trace (useful for large distributed traces).

References and links
- Accessibility checklist RFC: CONFSYS-4872
- Slack thread with initial ask: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C12345/p1678901234567
- Similar product inspiration: notes from 'fast-trace' internal workshop (link in Confluence)

Next steps for grooming meeting
- Bring prototype and demo for keyboard flows.
- Align on prefilter API contract with infra (how counts/sampling behave).
- Decide on initial keyboard shortcut set and ensure no conflicts with browser defaults or console-level shortcuts.
_notes: informal draft; lots of TODOs and placeholders for engineering. Designed to be a working doc for product + applied-ml + design to converge on a keyboard-first flow for the trace viewer.
